body:
John,

Your attempt to link Ted Turner with Kaczynski
is unfounded.  Ted Turner is a liberal.  Kaczynski
does not like liberals, and has expressly argued
that no leftists should be allowed to participate
in his hoped-for revolution.  You are right to
point to a Canadian Unabomber -- but the bomber
who argued in favor of individual rights and anarchy
was a fellow named Roger Bell.  He went under
the name of Loki7.  Arrested a year or two ago,
he's not talking.  His stationery had a swastika
emblazoned at the top.  The sort of stationery
a racialist might use.

The Unabomber makes very clear in his manifesto 
that he is not a leftist.  Shadow calculates that
2/9 of the manifesto is spent ranting against
leftists.  Have you read the manifesto?

Kaczynsi writes:
	[A] movement that exalts nature and opposes 
technology must take a resolutely anti-leftist 
stance and must avoid all collaboration with leftists. 
Leftism is in the long run inconsistent with wild nature, 
with human freedom and with the elimination of modern technology.  
	Industrial Society And Its Future, by ���FC��� (para. 214)

Most leftists, across the board, have disavowed him:
"Our power will come from organization, not killer 
tantrums."
		Christopher David Brady
		in misc.activism.progressive

Kaczynski defines "leftists" broadly:
	"When we speak of leftists in this article we have 
in mind mainly socialists, collectivists, "politically 
correct" types, feminists, gay and disability activists, 
animal rights activists and the like.   
	Industrial Society And Its Future, by ���FC��� (para. 7)

We also know of Dr. Kaczynski's hatred of leftists
from the FBI interviews:
	
"The source told BISCEGLIE that his parents were 
from a "leftist" background and that his brother 
lways had problems with them  about their views."
	FBI interview of Anthony P. Bisceglie on January 31, 1996 

Kaczynski sounded like Ayn Rand rolled into 
Rush Limbaugh, 
(See Alexander Cockburn in The Nation, dated 
August 28, 1995)  

Kaczynski writes:

	Leftists tend to hate anything that has an image of 
being strong,  good and successful.  They hate America, 
they hate Western civilization, they hate white males, 
they hate rationality.   
	Industrial Society And Its Future, by ���FC��� (para. 15)

Kaczynski writes about both leftists and neo-Nazis:
	
"Leftists, especially those of the oversocialized type, 
are True Believers in the sense of Eric Hoffer's book, 
The True Believer.  But not all True Believers are of 
the same psychological type as leftists.  Presumably a 
true-believing nazi, for instance, is very different psychologically from a
true-believing leftist.  
Because of their capacity for single-minded devotion to a cause, True Believers
are a useful, perhaps a necessary, ingredient of any revolutionary movement.   
	Industrial Society And Its Future, by ���FC��� (para. 222)

An articulate fellow named Bob McKeown summarized:

"The ideology of a violent Luddite would have 
inextricable links with neo-nazism, the survivalist 
movement and common law ideology.  The UB's ideology 
is *not* HD Thoreau -- although it's interesting 
to note the sympathy HD had for John Brown and violent abolitionism even as he
sat out the Mexican American war. "
	
John, do you consider yourself a racialist?  Some 
racialists have supported the Unabomber:	

	"It seems "Unabomber" has a very good understanding 
of not only leftists, but weak ass conservatives too, 
which would overlap to include many weak ass rightists 
as well.  I believe [he] has a much deeper understanding
 of our True human natures than the vast majority of 
people, and [that] understanding, along with his far-sightedness,  lead him to
write his/F.C.'s  manifesto.  
		Dannie Hawkins
		of W.A.R. [White Aryan Resistance]
		in alt.politics.greens

There is an excellent 1995 book called Eco-Fascism 
describing the environmental tradition among Nazis.  
You might also see the inaugural
issue of Metzger's W.A.R. newspaper in October 1993, 
or the essay "We are the real greens" by Milton Kleim 
(a former member of the National Alliance
who thinks McVeigh likely was framed).

You raise the question of similarities to the ideology
expressed by Gore (in Earth in the Balance).  That was
based on an unattributed source in the right-wing
"American Spectator."  (We'll assume it was accurate,
though the Spectator's admitted reliance on a single
source does not comport with sound journalistic standards.)
		
Dr. Kaczynski is anti-technology.  Gore is the Federal Government's main
advocate of information technology.  
They are ideologically opposed.

As "Jzgagne" said in newyorktimes.com forum 	
	
"The Bible talked about poverty, Das Capital by Karl Marx 
talked about poverty. I guess in your hallucinogenic 
world, either God is a communist or Karl Marx is God.  
Go back to your adventures of the right wing comic books."

Kaczynski himself writes to explain the difference
between him and the vast majority of radical 
environmentalists:
		
"Statements we made in our letters to associate 
us with anarchism and radical environmentalism, 
and therefore might make the public think of anarchists 
nd radical environmentalists as terrorists. So we 
want to make it clear that there is a NONVIOLENT 
anarchist movement that probably includes most 
people in America today who would describe 
themselves as anarchists.
	It's a safe bet that practically all of them 
strongly disapprove of our bombings.  Many radical environmentalists do engage
in sabotage, but the 
overwhelming majority of them are opposed to 
violence against human beings.	
Letter from ���FC��� to New York Times dated June 24, 1995

Admittedly, in addition to the letter you quote, 
searchers also found in the cabin a handwritten document 
entitled: ���How to hit an Exxon Exec��� which discussed 
sending a book-like package to the target���s home 
preceded by a letter.
	Government���s Trial Brief (Redacted Version), 
dated October 23, 1997

But Kaczynski left no room for confusion.  If anything,
he is clear and painstaking in his expression: 

"[N]ot all activist movements are leftist, and some 
activist movements (e.g., radical environmentalism) 
seem to include both personalities of the leftist type 
and personalities of thoroughly un-leftist types who 
ought to know better than to collaborate with leftists.
	Industrial Society And Its Future, by ���FC���  (para. 227)  
  
I'll end this overly long post with another quote
from Bob McKeown:

"Where I draw the line is placing him in the tradition 
of pure Luddites, who tend to be pacifists or 
religiously motivated or at least spiritual.  The 
radical engagement with the forces of destruction ala, 
say, Greenpeace, tends to be self-sacrificing.  
One lays oneself on the line in the battle.  This is 
where TK balks that tradition.   The profound 
individualism of TK's ideas are what I find so 
disturbing, and also what link them to a rightist 
rather than environmentalist tradition.
		Bobmckeown
		in newyorktimes.com forum

Instead, I'll end with someone better known, someone
who is a well-known Luddite :

"I should note that the Unabomber, on the evidence 
here, does not have  any special vision of an 
ecologically based future, as the newspapers 
have suggested.  Indeed, he is no environmentalist, 
and I'd say he has only the faintest grasp of the
principles of ecology.
���Unabomber���s Secret Treatise:  Is There Method 
In His Madness?,��� by Kirkpatrick Sale, The Nation, 
September 25, 1995
	
John, you seem a thoughtful well-read guy.  Do you
subscribe to any rightist periodicals?
